er_v06_c09_n101_01: A young woman comes to the window, her bracelet tapping the counter edge.
er_v06_c09_n101_02: Oh, this alley is even narrower than I thought.
er_v06_c09_n101_03: Walked all the way here, and my soles picked up three things. One I still don't want to identify.
er_v06_c09_n101_04: Had to ask three people to find this place. They all said yours is the only pawnshop on this street that doesn't cheat people.
er_v06_c09_n101_05: So tell me—does that count as a compliment?
er_v06_c09_n101_08: How many years have you been here?
er_v06_c09_n101_10: A few. Just minding a room full of old things.
er_v06_c09_n101_11: ...I didn't mean it like that. I talk fast. Don't take it to heart.
er_v06_c09_n101_12: She sets her bag on the counter, digs out a bracelet, fingers still pressed on it.
er_v06_c09_n101_13: Old thing. Found it at home.
er_v06_c09_n101_18: Really. Whatever you quote, I'll nod.
er_v06_c09_n102_01: The bracelet is turned over. A thin line of engraving runs inside the band.
er_v06_c09_n102_05: You're not going to ask where it came from?
er_v06_c09_n102_08: The bracelet goes into a wooden box under the counter. The lid snaps shut.
er_v06_c09_n102_09: You didn't try to cheat me on the price.
er_v06_c09_n102_10: I had a whole speech ready. Wasted.
er_v06_c09_n102_11: I figured if you pushed too hard, I'd know what to make of you.
er_v06_c09_n102_13: ...So I guess I'll ask the real question.
er_v06_c09_n102_14: Has a girl come by lately? Selling something?
er_v06_c09_n102_15: Upper-level accent, sharp tongue, about this tall, face longer than the shelves.
er_v06_c09_n102_18: We grew up together. After what happened to her mother, my family's door might as well have said don't mention it.
er_v06_c09_n102_19: I called her. Told her to come stay at my place.
er_v06_c09_n102_20: She answered with two words: no need. Then hung up.
er_v06_c09_n102_21: I was so mad I didn't sleep half the night. Next day I still texted her.
er_v06_c09_n102_22: She didn't answer a single one.
er_v06_c09_n102_24: I just want to know if she's been eating.
er_v06_c09_n102_26: Fine. I talk too much. I know.
er_v06_c09_n102_27: She slings the bag strap onto her shoulder and walks to the door.
er_v06_c09_n102_28: Leave the bracelet with you for now.
er_v06_c09_n102_29: I'll come redeem it in a few days.
er_v06_c09_n103_03: A friend. Her mother had trouble, she got sent down, won't see anyone.
er_v06_c09_n103_04: Once I say that, you should know who.
er_v06_c09_n103_05: She puts the bracelet back in her bag and fastens it.
er_v06_c09_n104_02: You didn't even check the quality before saying no.
er_v06_c09_n104_04: She puts the bracelet back in her bag. It takes her two tries to fasten the clasp.
er_v06_c10_n201_01: Eleanor comes to the window without speaking first.
er_v06_c10_n201_02: Yesterday afternoon, a woman left through this alley.
er_v06_c10_n201_03: Curly hair, new bag, doesn't watch where she walks.
er_v06_c10_n202_03: It's an old family piece. Her mother wore it.
er_v06_c10_n202_04: She actually pawned it down here.
er_v06_c10_n202_05: Did she ask you a pile of questions too?
er_v06_c10_n202_08: She says she's just visiting. Then goes home to tally how badly everyone else is doing, so she can feel she still has a conscience.
er_v06_c10_n202_09: ...Never mind. She's not a bad person.
er_v06_c10_n202_10: She just doesn't know what it's like down here.
er_v06_c10_n202_11: She rests her hand on the counter edge, fingertips scraping off a patch of old paint.
er_v06_c10_n203_03: ...Right. There's nothing for you two to talk about.
er_v06_c10_n203_04: People like her praise your stock when they arrive and forget it the moment they leave.
er_v06_c10_n204_03: Curly hair, new bag. Ten of those pass through this street a day.
er_v06_c10_n204_04: Her hand stops on the counter edge and stays there.
er_v06_c10_n204_05: ...I know her. Her name is Lydia.
er_v06_c10_n205_05: How would she know whether I eat.
er_v06_c10_n205_06: Twenty floors away, and she can count my meals?
er_v06_c10_n205_07: She never thinks before she talks.
er_v06_c10_n205_08: She looks down at the notch in the counter.
er_v06_c10_n205_14: ...I mean, don't sell it to anyone else.
er_v06_c10_n205_15: She'll come back for it. Lose something once, and she'll talk about it for half a year.
er_v06_c10_n205_17: Don't tell her where I live.
er_v06_c10_n205_20: I don't want her seeing the room I live in now.
er_v06_c10_n205_21: Across from the ration station, fourth floor, no light in the stairwell.
er_v06_c10_n205_22: If she stood in that doorway, I couldn't get a full sentence out.
er_v06_c10_n205_23: She sets the bag from her back onto the counter. It falls open, showing bits of shell and loose thread.
er_v06_c10_n205_26: Don't think I've changed. I just can't be bothered to do the math.
er_v06_c10_n206_01: The visitor stops at the window and looks around the shop through it.
er_v06_c10_n206_02: Heard you took in an old bracelet a few days ago.
er_v06_c10_n206_03: I'm not here for anything else. Just that.
er_v06_c10_n206_04: The wooden box goes onto the counter. The lid comes open.
er_v06_c10_n206_06: Old engraved pieces from upstairs—you see two a year, if that.
er_v06_c10_n206_07: Nobody hand-carves anymore. It's all machine-stamped. You can tell at a glance.
er_v06_c10_n206_12: Cash. Settled now. The money's right here.
er_v06_c10_n206_13: I won't go higher. If you're not short on money, pretend I never came.
er_v06_c10_n207_02: It's in your hands. Your call.
er_v06_c10_n207_03: If you change your mind, the price stays the same—and goes down.
er_v06_c10_n207_04: He pushes the box back half an inch and turns away from the window.
er_v06_c10_n208_01: The box is pushed over. The broker counts the money slowly.
er_v06_c10_n208_03: If you get more like this, come to me first.
er_v06_c10_n208_04: He wraps the bracelet in cloth and leaves without looking back.
er_v06_c10_n209_01: She comes to the window with a stack of money in her hand and stays standing.
er_v06_c10_n209_02: I'm here to redeem that bracelet.
er_v06_c10_n209_03: Five hundred. My own money, not the family's.
er_v06_c10_n209_04: I can manage that much. Don't turn your nose up at it.
er_v06_c10_n210_01: The bracelet is pushed over. Only the original amount is taken.
er_v06_c10_n210_03: I brought five hundred, and you take only that much. Now I don't know where to put my hands.
er_v06_c10_n210_04: Fine. I'll take the extra back. I won't be polite about it.
er_v06_c10_n211_02: You're just giving it to me?
er_v06_c10_n211_06: She takes the bracelet and says nothing more.
er_v06_c10_n212_02: If I go too low, will you think I'm taking advantage of you?
er_v06_c10_n212_03: ...Five hundred. That's it. Don't make me raise it.
er_v06_c10_n212_04: She pushes the money over and waits a moment before she gets the bracelet.
er_v06_c10_n213_02: My family reported it stolen last month.
er_v06_c10_n213_03: I took it from the cabinet. Really, just grabbed it. I was in a hurry that day.
er_v06_c10_n213_04: I figured no one would count what was in the drawer.
er_v06_c10_n213_05: Then my mother did inventory, item by item, and reported it.
er_v06_c10_n213_06: If I say I took it, I have to explain what I took it for.
er_v06_c10_n213_08: She slips the bracelet onto her wrist, turns it twice, and fastens the clasp.
er_v06_c10_n213_12: I went to see her twice. She wouldn't see me either time.
er_v06_c10_n213_13: First time I waited downstairs two hours. Second time she shut the door in my face.
er_v06_c10_n213_14: I stood at the stairwell, so dark I couldn't see the steps, and felt my way down.
er_v06_c10_n213_15: On the way out I kept thinking, she goes up and down those stairs every day.
er_v06_c10_n213_16: ...I never once thought about that before.
er_v06_c10_n213_18: I know plenty of people. I can ask around about things upstairs.
er_v06_c10_n213_19: How do you want to help.
er_v06_c10_n213_22: Let you two have a proper talk.
er_v06_c10_n213_23: She pulls her bag strap onto her shoulder, steps away from the window, then looks back.
er_v06_c10_n213_25: She walks away, the metal clasp on her bag clinking twice.
